cards.back: Basic rights and freedoms that belong to every person, regardless of nationality, sex, ethnicity, religion, or other status.

cards.front: What is the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
cards.back: A document adopted by the UN that sets out fundamental human rights to be universally protected.
The unjust or prejudicial treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, age, or sex.
The right to express one's opinions and ideas without fear of government retaliation or censorship.

cards.front: What is the right to education?
cards.back: The right of every person to have access to education without discrimination.
